claims.text: Introducing a low volume fraction of copper as finely dispersed, coherent nanoprecipitates will improve the thermal conductivity of the high-entropy alloy.
The copper nanoprecipitates will preserve the alloy's mechanical integrity under plasma-facing conditions.
Incorporating approximately 5 wt% copper through co-melting and tailored thermal treatments can form nanoscale, coherent copper precipitates in the alloy matrix.
The proposed benefit will occur during operation between approximately 500°C and 800°C under cyclic mechanical loading.
A nanoscale dispersion of coherent copper precipitates will furnish an interconnected heat-transport network.
The proposed precipitate network will enhance electron and phonon heat transport.
Coherent nanoscale copper precipitates will avoid forming detrimental stress concentrators.
Copper has high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Nanoscale copper precipitates promote heat transfer through electronic and phononic channels.
Coherency between the copper precipitates and matrix permits thermal bridging.
Coherent copper precipitates will not significantly alter the grain-boundary structure responsible for mechanical strength.
The modified alloy will exhibit approximately 10–20% greater thermal conductivity than the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will maintain yield strength comparable to the unmodified baseline under the specified conditions.
The modified alloy will maintain ductility comparable to the unmodified baseline under the specified conditions.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers without copper microalloying have lower thermal conductivity but acceptable structural integrity.
Prolonged extreme temperatures or excessive radiation doses may cause copper precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency may compromise performance.
